summary: The new axion-electron bound g_ae < 1.49e-13 at 95% C.L. from the distance-independent TRGB-RGBB method (Levasseur et al. 2026) is correctly identified, genuinely new, confidence-supported, convention-consistent, and numerically matches the paper (abstract, Sec.7, Fig.14). The new limit's defining boundary is shown and labeled. Only minor, non-blocking display issues remain (label crowding vs. the existing omega-Cen entry and shared crimson color with Solar nu in the highlighted view).

verdict.summary: The new axion-electron bound g_ae < 1.49e-13 at 95% C.L. from the distance-independent TRGB-RGBB method (Levasseur et al. 2026) is correctly identified, genuinely new, confidence-supported, convention-consistent, and numerically matches the paper (abstract, Sec.7, Fig.14). The new limit's defining boundary is shown and labeled. Only minor, non-blocking display issues remain (label crowding vs. the existing omega-Cen entry and shared crimson color with Solar nu in the highlighted view).

result_identity.evidence: Paper title and abstract (p.1): constraint on axion-electron coupling g_ae from RGB stars. extraction coupling_type=AxionElectron, g_ae dimensionless. Exclusion (is_projection=false), new measured bound. Matches.

novelty.evidence: 2026 preprint presenting a NEW distance-independent (TRGB-RGBB magnitude difference) method on 47 Tuc, NGC 362, M5 yielding a new combined 95% bound (abstract; Sec.3,7). Distinct independent measurement, not an old bound re-quoted. Note: slightly weaker than existing Red giants (omega-Cen) ~1.3e-13, but a genuine new measurement.

confidence_level.evidence: Abstract and Sec.7 (p.12): explicit '95% C.L. upper limit of 1.49', a Bayesian 95% upper credible bound with uniform g13 prior (Fig.14). extraction confidence_level=0.95 is paper-supported, not a default/placeholder.

conventions.evidence: g_ae standard dimensionless (p.2). Axion treated massless/light; production suppressed near core thermal energy T~8.6 keV (p.2). Mass-independent flat line in eV; data file 1.49e-13 with no density/polarization needed. Upper cutoff 1e4 eV is extractor's representation choice (~core temperature), reasonable; lower start 1e-11 eV is a representation choice.

numerical_agreement.evidence: Data points fixed at g_ae=1.49e-13, matching the headline 95% WL2011 combined bound (abstract; Sec.7 p.12; Fig.14 dashed line at g13=1.49). MARCS alternative 1.62 and per-cluster 1.99/1.92/2.03 also consistent with the paper.

highlight_target.evidence: Highlighted PNG shows the new RGB limit's defining lower boundary at ~1.49e-13 spanning 1e-11 to 1e4 eV with the red 'R(GB)' label at bottom-left, matching the data. Correct target accented. (Advisory: the pre-existing crimson 'Solar nu' region shares the accent color and also appears red.)

visibility.evidence: Boundary at 1.49e-13 is on-screen across the relevant mass range and labeled 'RGB'. (Advisory: nearly coincident with existing Red giants omega-Cen ~1.3e-13, so the full-view label is cramped/partly clipped; interpretable via the highlighted view.)

findings.description: In the highlighted view, the pre-existing 'Solar nu' exclusion shares the crimson highlight color and also renders red, so it is co-accented alongside the new RGB limit.
findings.evidence: AxionElectron_highlighted.png shows a large stepped red region matching the Solar nu shape (flat ~8e-9 then rising to ~7e-6 at THz with QUAX vertical features) in addition to the RGB boundary at 1.49e-13.
findings.requested_change: Optionally assign the new RGB limit a highlight color distinct from the compilation's crimson so only the new result is accented.

findings.description: New bound (1.49e-13) is nearly coincident with and slightly weaker than the existing Red giants (omega-Cen) entry (~1.3e-13); the full-view 'RGB' label is crowded/partly obscured.
findings.evidence: AxionElectron.png: only 'R' is visible at the far-left ~1e-13, overlapping 'Red giants (omega-Cen)' text.
findings.requested_change: Optionally reposition/resize the RGB label for legibility; no scientific change needed.

findings.description: The flat line's mass extent (1e-11 to 1e4 eV) is the extractor's representation choice, not stated by the paper.
findings.evidence: extraction notes acknowledge the 1e4 eV upper cutoff is chosen (~core temperature 8.6 keV, p.2); paper quotes no explicit mass range.
findings.requested_change: None required; the choice is physically reasonable, but curators should be aware the endpoints are conventions, not paper values.
